messages:
maya: Quick Q — we're moving TLS termination off the ALB and doing TLS passthrough with Gateway API (TLSRoute passthrough) so services handle mTLS. What do I need to change in the Service + Terraform bits? Anyone done cert-manager + app-side mTLS behind an NLB-style passthrough?

liam: i've done a similar setup. main things: LB must be TCP passthrough (no TLS termination), Service should expose NodePort/LoadBalancer with backend protocol tcp, and externalTrafficPolicy: Local if you need client IP preserved and to make healthchecks work. also ensure targetPort matches the container port (very common mismatch).

serena: +1. For AWS NLB via Service of type LoadBalancer use annotations like: `service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"` and set backend protocol to tcp. Example snippet:```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: my-mtls-svc
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tcp"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  ports:
  - port: 443
    targetPort: 8443
    protocol: TCP
  selector:
    app: my-mtls-app
```

serena: certs are managed by cert-manager in the app namespace — the LB doesn't need a cert since it's passthrough. make sure your Deployment listens on the TLS port and has the cert secret mounted (or uses a sidecar).

liam: terraform bits — ensure the Kubernetes service resource preserves annotations in the module that creates LBs. if you're using an infra module that assumes ALB, it might overwrite backend-protocol or add ssl-listener config. i opened a quick PR to the infra module to add a `nlb_passthrough` flag and preserve tcp annotations: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra-aws/pull/462 (link for context only).

maya: thanks — what about Gateway API config? do we need to attach secrets to the Gateway resource even if passthrough?

serena: for TLSRoute passthrough the Gateway shouldn't have the secret for TLS termination. You do need a GatewayClass and a Gateway that accepts TLSRoute with passthrough backendRefs. The TLS credentials live with the service (app) when doing mTLS. Example TLSRoute snippet:```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: TLSRoute
metadata:
  name: mtls-passthrough
spec:
  parentRefs:
  - name: my-gateway
  hostnames:
  - "*.example.internal"
  rules:
  - backendRefs:
    - name: my-mtls-svc
      port: 443
```

liam: small ops gotcha: AWS NLB healthchecks are by default TCP; if you configure an HTTP healthcheck accidentally you'll fail. Also double-check `targetType` on the AWS side (ip vs instance) depending on whether you're using ip target type with CNI.

infra-automation-bot: reminder: run `make infra-validate` in the infra repo after updating the service module; CI will catch missing annotations (runs in ~6m).

oncall-bot: incident note — if Gateway provider fails to bind TLSRoute, traffic will fall back to default LB behavior. consider a canary route weight or an automatic fallback to ALB for critical services.

serena: for canary you can create two Gateways (gateway-a = passthrough, gateway-b = alb-terminated) and use route selection by labels/weights in your rollout job so you can move traffic back quickly. keep healthcheck endpoints consistent so probes behave the same.

maya: perfect, that's enough to unblock the PR. i'll update the service manifest + terraform module flag and ping in this thread for review. :thumbsup:

liam: cheers — ping me once PR is up, i'll review the annotations + targetPort checks.

serena: happy to review Gateway YAML. make sure cert-manager issuer is in the same namespace as the app.

maya: will do, thx all.
